pages.title: Get Started - Red Shed
pages.text:
Get Started
Everyone at Red Shed started somewhere. Most people arrive one of three ways, so pick the door that sounds like you.
Just curious? Try the Starter Pack.
Three sessions for $30, valid 30 days, to use across rowing, the gym and recovery in any mix. No membership, no commitment, and you’re set up in our booking system from day one. It’s the easiest way to find out what Red Shedder life feels like.
Try the Starter Pack
Here for the water? Start with a rowing program.
Never rowed before? Learn to Row takes you from first stroke to first crew on Lake Burley Griffin. Rowed years ago or still rowing now? Continue to Row finds you a seat. Year 7 to 12 in the family? Our youth programs are the place to start.
Explore rowing programs
Ready to jump in? Become a Red Shedder.
One membership, the whole shed: rowing, RSX Strength Club and the recovery hub, with a tier to match how often you’ll come. Every membership includes the community that makes this place what it is.
Choose your membership
Still deciding? Drop in for a
casual visit
, or just come and say hi. Coffee, matcha and easy eats served from 7am to 2pm at
Easy Oar
, 7 days a week.

pages.text:
Row
Rowing for all
Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced athlete, our expert-led rowing caters to every age, ability and ambition. Rowing for All is our mission, and it starts here.
From first stroke to first crew
Every Red Shedder started somewhere. Our coaches take you from your first stroke to your first crew, on the calm of Lake Burley Griffin.
Two ways to row
Through a program
Our fixed-length rowing programs are how most people begin. Each is a single program fee, run by our coaches. Some start from your very first stroke; others build on experience. Everyone in our youth programs rows this way, in term time or across the school holidays.
See the programs
As a Red Shedder
For experienced rowers and our Learn to Row graduates: timetabled rowing sessions are part of your weekly membership allowance, alongside the gym and recovery. Book through Mindbody and row as often as your tier allows. Memberships are for adults 18 and over, so youth rowers come to us through programs instead.
See memberships

Where everyone starts: beginner programs for adults, youth and university students, no experience needed.
Learn to Row
Continue to Row
Development and Squad sessions that keep you building after your first program.

pages.text:
Learn to Row
Learn to Row is where rowing starts at Red Shed, for adults and youth alike. Programs are run by accredited Red Shed coaches on the calm water of Lake Burley Griffin. No experience needed: we take you from your very first stroke to rowing confidently in a crew. If you like the full picture before you book, start with our
Learn to Row guide
.
Adults
For complete beginners, no experience or fitness prerequisites
Small groups with accredited coaches
See adult course dates
Youth
For students in Years 7 to 12
See youth term dates
See youth holiday dates
What you’ll get
Expert coaching, quality equipment and practical feedback every session
The technique and confidence to keep rowing after the program
A friendly group of fellow beginners, on the best training water in Australia
Studying?
We also run a Learn to Row program specifically for university students, at a student rate, and it is open to students from any university. Look for the uni student listing in the course dates below, or email
info@redshed.org.au
and we will point you to the next one.

pages.title: Continue to Row - Red Shed
pages.text:
Continue to Row
You’ve learned to row, now it’s about getting better. Continue to Row brings together our
Development
and
Squad
programs for adults, so you can progress at your own pace in a crew that pushes you along.
Adults
Development
: refine your stroke and grow as an all-round rower
Squad
: advanced coaching and race preparation
Covered by a
Red Shedder Membership
, with
casual sessions and 10-passes
too
Adult programs
Youth
Youth have their own pathway: development, squad, elite and private coaching
It all lives on our Youth & School Programs page
Youth & school programs
The programs
Development
For rowers ready to refine their stroke and build confidence across a range of boats.
Sharpen technique in team boats and single sculls
Build crew cohesion and fitness
Grow into a versatile, self-sufficient rower
Squad
For seasoned rowers training with intent.
Advanced coaching, race strategy, pacing and endurance
Structured group sessions with like-minded rowers
Entry requirement:
pass a capsize test in a single and gain sign-off from our coaching team
University students
We run programs specifically for uni students, from any university, at a student rate. If you rowed at school and want to keep going, or you are starting from scratch, see
Learn to Row
or get in touch.
Racing and club rowing
Black Mountain Rowing Club
is Red Shed’s home club and where most of our rowers go when they want to race. It’s for experienced rowers, so it isn’t the step straight out of Learn to Row, but keep building through development and it’s a natural place to end up. There are other clubs around Canberra too, and your coach can talk you through what suits you.
How it works
Development and Squad sessions are covered by a
Red Shedder Membership*
. Prefer to pay as you go?
Casual sessions and 10-session passes
are available, and you can buy either before you come. Session times live in the timetable, book via Mindbody.
What’s on this week
Development and Squad sessions both appear in the timetable below. Pick a session that suits your week and book it.
Nothing on the list that suits?
Leave your details and we will let you know when new Continuing to Row sessions are added.

pages.text:
Camps & Clinics
For rowers who want to go further, adults and youth. Our performance programs bring expert coaching, quality equipment and practical feedback to the beautiful waterways of Canberra.
Adults
3 Day Performance Clinic
: intensive skills work with our senior coaches
Masters Performance Intensive
: focused blocks for masters rowers
Private coaching
: one-on-one, built around your goals
Adult programs
Youth
School holiday programs
: on-water camps in every school break
Winter Elite
: high-performance training for invited athletes
Entry by invitation, register your interest
School Holiday Programs
Winter Elite
Adults
Programs
Masters Performance Intensive
, focused blocks for masters rowers
Performance clinics
, short, intensive skills work
Private coaching
, one-on-one, built around your goals
Each is a fixed-length program with its own fee, booked separately from a membership.
The 3 Day Performance Clinic
Lake Burley Griffin is Australia’s National Training Centre for Olympic rowing, and Red Shed runs more Learn-to-Row sessions than any other club in Australia. Our performance programs put that same water and coaching to work on your racing.
Three days with Red Shed’s senior coaching team: video analysis on the laned race course, targeted drills that turn the assessment into change on the water, and a big-boat row on Lake Burley Griffin, with recovery built in between sessions. The
3 Day Performance Clinic guide
covers how the days run, who it suits, what’s included and what to bring.
Masters Performance Intensive
A focused block for masters rowers with Red Shed’s senior coaching team. The
Masters Performance Intensive guide
covers how it runs, who it suits and what to bring.
Current dates and prices
are always up to date in the booking widget below.
Book via Mindbody
Enquire / register your interest
Upcoming dates
Register your interest
No dates showing yet? Leave your details and we will tell you the moment the next camp or clinic opens.
Clinics for your club
Bring your club to Red Shed. We build clinics around what your crews actually need, whether that is technical work with video, rigging, race preparation or a full weekend on Lake Burley Griffin. You tell us the squad, the level and the goal, and we design the program around it.
Coached by our senior rowing team, on the water your athletes want to race on
Access to our race weight fleet, or bring your own boats
Recovery hub, cafe and function space on site, so a visiting squad has everything in one place
Email
rowing@redshed.org.au
with your club, your numbers and roughly when you are thinking, and we will come back with options.
After your program
Want to know more?
Both programs have a full guide covering how the days run, who they suit, what to bring and what you take home. Read the
3 Day Performance Clinic guide
or the
Masters Performance Intensive guide
.
Finished your program? A Red Shedder Membership* keeps you going, across the gym, the water and the recovery hub, with automatic Red Shedder benefits including complimentary Resets and member events.
See the memberships

Slow mornings, fresh plates, good coffee and food made to be grabbed, shared and enjoyed before the day runs away. pages.title: Red Shed FAQs: membership, booking, access
pages.text:
FAQs
Memberships & passes
What is a Red Shedder Membership?
One membership for the whole shed. Your tier gives you a weekly allowance of sessions to use across rowing, the gym and recovery, in any mix, plus automatic Red Shedder benefits like complimentary Resets and member events. Tiers are Copper $35, Bronze $55, Silver $69, Gold $99 and Platinum $119 per week, with a 12-week minimum term. For recovery only, there is also a dedicated
Recovery membership
at $45 per week.
What is the Starter Pack?
The Starter Pack is 3 sessions for $30, valid 30 days, across rowing, gym or recovery. It’s a taste of Red Shedder membership life, not a program.
Do I have to hold a membership to visit?
No. Casual visits and 10-packs are available, and Easy Oar, Resets and community events are open to everyone.
See casual visits & 10-packs
.
Is there a BMRC option?
Yes. If you row competitively, Black Mountain Rowing Club (BMRC) operates at Red Shed. A BMRC Partner option connects club membership with facility access.
Ask us
and we’ll point you the right way.
Can I get a membership refund?
Refunds and cancellations follow our published terms and conditions. See Terms & Conditions or ask us at
info@redshed.org.au
.
Booking & sessions
How do I book?
Everything is booked through Mindbody, including rowing, gym and recovery sessions and our programs. Set yourself up once and book whatever suits your week.
How do I book a rowing session on the Starter Pack?
Rowing on the Starter Pack requires prior rowing experience or a completed Learn to Row. If you’re brand new to rowing, start with
Learn to Row
first.
I’m not a rower. Can I still join?
Absolutely. Plenty of Red Shedders come for the gym, recovery and community and never pick up an oar, and Learn to Row runs all year if you’d like to try.
Facility & hours
What are the opening hours?
The Red Shed facility is open to Red Shedders 5am to 8pm daily. Rowing and gym sessions run per the Mindbody timetable. Showers and facilities are available 5am to 8pm daily, no booking needed. Recovery runs 5am to 8pm daily with a booking. Casual recovery visits (no fob) are 9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday. Easy Oar is 7am to 2pm daily.
Full guide
.
What is fob access?
Red Shedders and 10-pack holders get a fob for access any time 5am to 8pm daily. Casual visitors without a fob can come in 9am to 5pm on weekdays.
Where are you, and is there parking?
45 John Cardiff Close, Acton ACT 2601, on Black Mountain Peninsula. Free parking is available. The peninsula gate closes, so please leave before closing time.
Programs
What programs do you run?
Coaching is provided for every Red Shed program. Options run from Learn to Row through to high performance, plus youth, school holiday, social, corporate and tourism rowing.
See Row
.
Which program is right for me?
If you’re new, start with Learn to Row. From there, Continue to Row and Return to Row help you keep going, and performance programs are there when you want to push further. Not sure? Email
info@redshed.org.au
.
Can I race for Red Shed?
Red Shed doesn’t enter crews at regattas. Rowers who want to race do it through a club, and
Black Mountain Rowing Club
is where most of ours go.
Support & community
How can I support Red Shed?
Red Shed is a not-for-profit built to make rowing, movement and wellbeing possible for everyone, and it exists thanks to private donations. Donations are fully tax deductible through the Australian Sports Foundation. For donations, sponsorship or partnership, email
info@redshed.org.au
.
Support Red Shed
.
Can I volunteer?
Yes, and we’d love the help. From events to Golden Oar to rowing programs, there’s a role for you.
Volunteer
.
Thinking about learning to row? Our
Learn to Row guide
covers what to wear, how sessions run and where rowing takes you next, including answers to many of our Learn to Row FAQs.
Ready when you are
Still got questions? The easiest answer is to come and feel it for yourself.

Red Shed Terms of Use
Effective as of: 16 June 2025
1
Participation Agreement
By
participating
in any program, event, or service offered by Red Shed Inc — including but not limited to rowing programs, gym access and classes, wellness services and bookings, community events, social functions, and café-related activities — individuals agree to abide by these terms and conditions and the accompanying
participant waiver
.
What a Red Shedder Membership is
A Red Shedder Membership is a subscription that provides access to Red Shed facilities, programmes, services and activities in accordance with the applicable Membership Terms and Conditions. It is a contractual right of participation only and does not confer membership of Red Shed Incorporated or any rights of membership of that association, whether under its constitution or governing legislation.
2
Participant Waiver
By booking into any Red Shed Inc service, participants acknowledge that they’ve read and understood the Participant Waiver available in the relevant event, service, or program description.
CLICK HERE TO VIEW THE PARTICIPANT WAIVER
3
Health and Safety
Participants must ensure they are in good health and free from any medical conditions that could affect safe participation. It is strongly recommended that participants seek medical advice before beginning any new fitness or wellness routine.
Participants must notify Red Shed Inc in writing of any changes to their physical or mental health that may impact their participation. Red Shed Inc reserves the right to arrange emergency medical treatment — including first aid, defibrillation, ambulance, or safety boat transport — and participants agree to bear all related costs.
4
Assumption of Risk
Participation in Red Shed Inc services involves inherent risks. These include, but are not limited to:
Physical activities: rowing, gym use, exercise classes;
Recovery services: cold plunge, traditional Finnish sauna, infrared sauna, dry float bed, EMS (Electronic Muscle Stimulation), Normatec compression therapy, and other similar offerings;
Community and social events.
Participants acknowledge risks such as death, serious physical or mental injury, disease, and economic loss. Physical injury risks include drowning, head/neck/spinal trauma, damage to musculoskeletal and internal systems. Mental injury risks may include psychological harm or psychiatric illness.
5
Booking and Cancellation
Bookings
Bookings are essential for all services at Red Shed, including but not limited to:
Rowing programs and classes;
Gym access and group sessions;
Wellness services and appointments;
Community events and private functions.
The café usually accepts walk-ins depending on availability each day.
Some services, such as café operations, may allow walk-in access where applicable.
Cancellation & Refunds
Notice periods and suspensions apply to Red Shedder Agreements only. Programs are paid in advance and are non-refundable.
If Red Shed cancels a program
If Red Shed cancels a whole program, you will be offered a transfer, credit or refund for that program. Individual sessions affected by weather or events outside our control are moved indoors or rescheduled under our weather policy rather than cancelled.
All cancellation or credit requests must be made in writing via
info@redshed.org.au
.
Red Shed’s cancellation and refund policy depends on the type of agreement, program or pass that has been arranged. Please see below for full details:
Red Shedder Agreements (ongoing facility and class access)
Red Shedder arrangements have a minimum commitment period of 12 weeks, after which they continue on a rolling basis until cancelled.
Cancellations require a minimum of 4 weeks’ written notice. Payments continue during the notice period.
Suspensions are permitted for a minimum of 2 weeks and a maximum of 8 weeks per calendar year. Suspension does not constitute notice of cancellation.
Programs
Program enrolments are paid in advance to secure your place and are
non-refundable
. This covers all our programs, including Learn to Row, term-based rowing, school holiday programs, camps, clinics and intensives, and applies whether or not you attend every session.
Casual Bookings
Cancellations for all casual bookings (e.g. drop-in gym or wellness use) must be made at least
24 hours in advance
to avoid being charged the full session fee.
Private Coaching and Personal Training
Cancellations for private sessions (e.g. private rowing, PT, recovery coaching) must be made at least
24 hours in advance
. Cancellations made within 24 hours will be charged at the full rate.
In the event of adverse weather, Red Shed’s weather policy still applies. Red Shed will make every effort to substitute with an appropriate indoor or alternative activity.
Red Shed reserves the right to update cancellation windows in specific coaching agreements or seasonal programs.
Medical Considerations
If a participant is unable to attend due to a verified medical issue:
We may consider applying a
credit
toward future services, subject to written notification and supporting documentation (e.g. medical certificate).
Refunds are not guaranteed and will be assessed on a case-by-case basis by Red Shed management.
All cancellation or credit requests must be made in writing via
info@redshed.org.au
.
6
Failed Payments
If a scheduled payment is declined or otherwise fails, Red Shed may:
Charge a dishonour fee (where applicable);
Retry the payment;
Suspend access to facilities, services, or bookings until the account is brought up to date;
Recover any outstanding amounts, including through a third-party provider if required.
7
Late Pickup Policy
This policy applies to all youth programs. Parents/guardians must collect children on time. A fee of $15 per 15 minutes (or part thereof) applies for late pickups. This must be paid before the child may attend again.
If a child is permitted to leave independently, express permission must be granted in two ways:
In writing via email in advance;
and
Confirmed in person with a Red Shed staff member on the first day of the program.
8
Supervision and Instruction
Participants must follow all reasonable instructions provided by Red Shed staff and coaches. Failure to comply may increase the risk of injury and could lead to removal from a session or program.
Red Shed reserves the right to restrict access or participation based on a failure to follow instructions related to safety or group management.
9
Use of Facilities and Equipment
Participants must treat all facilities and equipment responsibly. Any damage caused through misuse or negligence may result in financial liability for repair or replacement, or restricted access.
Red Shed recognises that damage may occur as part of regular use. If an item or space is damaged or unsafe, participants are required to notify staff immediately. A simple reporting process (QR code or online form) will be made available on the noticeboard and other key locations within the facility.
10
Weather Policy
Weather may impact some activities, particularly rowing. Where outdoor activities are deemed unsafe due to heat, wind, storms, air quality, or other factors, Red Shed reserves the right to:
Modify or relocate activities with little or no notice;
Substitute with an appropriate alternative activity (indoors, outdoors, or otherwise) aimed at delivering similar value or skill development;
Not offer a refund or credit due to weather-related changes.
Safety remains our priority, and decisions may be made on the day or immediately prior to sessions.
11
Code of Conduct
Participants are expected to uphold the values and standards outlined in the Red Shed Code of Conduct.
Red Shed Code of Conduct
.
Failure to comply may result in warnings, suspension, or removal from a program, class, or the facility.
12
Personal Belongings
Red Shed Inc is not responsible for any loss or damage to belongings brought onsite. Participants are encouraged to store valuables in designated areas or lockers.
Day-use lockers unlock automatically after 3 hours. Permanent lockers are available to hire on a month-to-month basis — please enquire at reception for details.
13
Photography and Marketing
Red Shed Inc may photograph or film participants during sessions or events for promotional use. If you do not wish to appear in such material, please advise staff in writing before the session begins. Further information is available in Red Shed’s Privacy Policy.
Red Shed (or authorised third parties) may store, publish, or reuse imagery for Red Shed–related promotion without compensation. Removal requests can be made via
info@redshed.org.au
.
14
Surveillance of Venues
All Red Shed facilities and equipment are subject to ongoing video and audio surveillance. This includes gym spaces, rowing sheds, common areas, recovery zones, and entrances.
While surveillance systems are maintained for safety and compliance purposes, Red Shed cannot guarantee the availability or clarity of footage at all times. Any footage linked to suspected misconduct may be shared with law enforcement or relevant authorities.
15
Privacy
Red Shed collects personal information to provide services and manage participation. This includes registration, safety records, and communication.
By enrolling, participants consent to the collection and use of their personal information in accordance with Red Shed’s
Privacy Policy.
16
Intellectual Property
All Red Shed Inc content, branding, and operational frameworks — including but not limited to digital content, training materials, written programs, session structures, marketing assets, and in-person experiences — remain the property of Red Shed Inc.
These are protected under relevant intellectual property laws and may not be copied, reproduced, or used commercially without permission.
17
Modifications and Amendments
These terms may be updated periodically. Red Shed will publish major changes on our website and notify members by email where
appropriate
.
18
Governing Law
These terms and conditions shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Australian Capital Territory (ACT), Australia. Any disputes arising out of or related to these terms and conditions shall be resolved exclusively through the courts of the ACT, Australia.
By engaging with any Red Shed program, service, or facility, you confirm that you have read, understood, and
agree
to these Terms and Conditions.

Nick Galea
Director of Rowing
Nick joined Red Shed in November 2025 from Glebe Rowing Club in Sydney, where he built a thriving youth and masters program. He has developed state champions, coached youth rowers who went on to national representation, and masters rowers who have won medals at international competition. Nick believes in the inclusion of all ages and abilities in rowing.
Sarah Peterswald
Rowing Operations Manager
Sarah is a full-time rowing coach at Red Shed and sits on the coaching team for the ACT Interstate senior team and the youth pathways program. A Canberra native, she rowed and coached at Canberra Grammar before coaching in Northern Ireland and Oxford. She also holds a double degree in Design and Commerce from ANU.
Charlotte McCarthy
Rowing and Fitness Coach
Charlotte is a full-time rowing coach and gym trainer at Red Shed, combining years of practical rowing experience with a Bachelor of Exercise Science to support athlete development. She coaches our Junior Red Shed Scholarship athletes, who recently medalled at the NSW State Championships and are preparing for Nationals.
Lyall McCarthy OAM
Rowing Coach
Lyall coached Kim Brennan to Olympic gold in the single scull at Rio 2016, one of four Olympic medals he has coached across three Games, alongside multiple world championship titles. Appointed Australia’s head women’s rowing coach at the AIS in Canberra in 1997 and later Rowing Australia’s Pathways Head Coach, he received an OAM for service to rowing in 2018. At Red Shed he takes private sessions on request, coaches across selected programs, and mentors our coaching team rather than running a regular squad.

Coach and Lead Volunteer

He also serves as Secretary on the Red Shed committee.

pages.title: Mission & Values - Red Shed
pages.text:
Mission & Values
Red Shed is a not-for-profit incorporated association that opened in July 2024. We exist to use rowing, movement and community as tools for positive change in Canberra, breaking down the barriers that keep people off the water and out of good health.
Our mission, in three parts
Rowing for All.
Breaking down socioeconomic and physical barriers to make rowing accessible, through adaptive programs, youth scholarships and learn-to-row opportunities.
Inspiring Wellness.
A strength gym, recovery spaces and wellbeing hubs that support physical and mental health.
Fostering Community.
A gathering place, with a cafe, event spaces and volunteer programs, where anyone can belong.
Our values
Community
: we’re better together, and everyone is welcome.
Commitment
: we show up, for our people and our mission.
Opportunity
: we open doors that were closed, and create pathways that last.
Fun
: because the best things in life feel good.
Not for profit
Red Shed is a not-for-profit built to make rowing, movement and wellbeing possible for everyone. We’re funded by program fees, Easy Oar, Telopea Room functions and the generosity of donors, and every contribution keeps the shed open to all. Donations through the Australian Sports Foundation are fully tax deductible.

Functions & Events
Red Shed is at capacity for functions in 2026
We brought our food and beverage in house this year and we are not taking any new function bookings for 2026. We will open 2027 bookings later this year. Corporate rowing is unaffected and still running, see
Corporate & Team Building
. Leave your email below and we will let you know the moment we do.
The Telopea Room is Red Shed’s function space, right on Lake Burley Griffin. Floor-to-ceiling windows, flexible layouts and in-house catering from Easy Oar make it one of Canberra’s most memorable places to gather.
Made for
Corporate events, meetings and away-days
Celebrations and private functions
Team building, on land or on the water
Space and facilities
The Telopea Room
Seats up to 160, or up to 220 standing, with flexible table layouts
In-house catering from morning teas to canapés and shared-style three-course dinners
Two 100-inch screens, handheld, lapel and lectern microphones, BOSE sound and a hearing loop
Just 8 minutes from the CBD, with on-site parking
The Co-Working Room
A private boardroom seating up to 10
Optional food and beverage service from Easy Oar
TV, camera and microphone for hybrid meetings
Book it on its own, or add it to a Telopea Room event
The Outdoor Space
The concrete waterfront apron between the boat shed and the pontoons, covered by our licence
A lakeside setting for ceremonies, welcome drinks or a marquee
Available as an add-on to a Telopea Room event
Choose your occasion
Corporate & team building
Weddings
Birthdays & private functions
Wellness workshops
Corporate & team building
Add rowing, a gym session or recovery to your event. Bring your team down to try rowing on the lake, then recover in the sauna and eat at Easy Oar. We’ll build the day around you.
Download the room layouts (PDF)
Ready-made packages
Tell us the occasion and the numbers, and we’ll send a per-person proposal. Popular shapes:
Full corporate day
: rowing on the lake, food and drinks, and a wellness session
Half day
: morning row, breakfast and a workshop
Conference
: the Telopea Room with AV and catering breaks
Wellness day
: yoga, breathwork, sauna and cold plunge
Rowing experience
: an on-water session, then coffee at Easy Oar
Corporate rowing
RSX
Recovery
Catering
From morning teas to canapés and shared-style three-course sit-down dinners, catering is handled in-house by Easy Oar using fresh, seasonal local produce.
Choose the style that suits your event, from shared feasting menus that bring the whole table together, to canapés for a standing, mingling crowd.
Register your interest
We are not taking function bookings for 2026 and we cannot provide availability or quotes until later this year. Leave your name and email and you will be first to hear when 2027 bookings open.
Follow
@redshedcbr.events
on Instagram: weddings, corporate days and the Telopea Room dressed up.

How many people does the Telopea Room hold?
It depends how you want to use it. On round tables it seats 160, or 100 once you add a band and a dance floor. Long tables seat 104. Theatre style for a presentation takes 160, classroom style 36, and a U shape 35. For a stand-up cocktail event the room holds 220 standing, and it can be split into two spaces of 24.
Download the room layouts
for a drawing of each configuration. Final numbers depend on staging, catering style, AV and access, so treat these as a starting point rather than a promise.
Is the deck ours for the event?
Not exclusively. The outdoor deck is shared with the Easy Oar cafe, so it stays open to cafe customers while your event is on. It is a lovely space to spill out into. We just want you to know it is not private.
What sorts of events do you host?
Some event types are not available or require additional security. Tell us what you have in mind.
When do bookings for 2027 open?
Later this year. We have not set a date, because we want the kitchen running exactly as it should be before we take on more events. Join the list and you will hear from us as soon as we know.
Who does the catering?
The Easy Oar kitchen, in house. Bringing food and beverage in house this year is the reason we have paused new function bookings, and it is why the wait will be worth it.

pages.title: Sustainability - Red Shed
pages.text:
Sustainability
People + Planet + Performance. The Red Shed sustainability strategy.
We believe in the transformative power of rowing. It builds community, drives personal development, nurtures diversity and fosters belonging, a foundation for growth. Transformation takes vision, commitment and drive for the long term. That drive sits behind everything we do, including our critical focus on sustainability.
We deliver our mission by sustaining our people and our planet, with a careful eye on performance.
One strategy, three commitments
01 People. Better, together.
Sustainability starts with a community that everyone can join, belong to and grow in, whatever “better” means to you.
Inclusion and belonging.
Programs and spaces designed for all ages, abilities and backgrounds. No experience needed to start.
Youth pathways.
Learn to Row programs for years 7 to 12 that build confidence, teamwork and lifelong healthy habits.
Health and wellbeing.
Rowing, training, recovery and connection in one place, supporting physical and mental wellbeing.
Our people.
Investing in the staff, coaches and volunteers who make Red Shed what it is, so they can find their better too.
02 Planet. A better way to care for our place.
Our lakeside setting is the heart of everything we do. Sustaining it is not a side project. It’s how we protect what makes Red Shed better.
Energy and emissions.
Reducing our footprint through on-site renewable energy, efficient equipment and smarter use of our facilities.
Waste and circularity.
Cutting single-use items across the site and cafe, prioritising reusables, recycling and responsible procurement.
Water and lake stewardship.
Caring for the water we row on: responsible water use, and protecting the lake’s foreshore and habitat.
Sustainable food.
A cafe philosophy built on wellness and low-waste operations, with local sourcing wherever we can.
03 Performance. Better for the long run.
Lasting impact needs a strong organisation behind it. Performance is how we make sure People and Planet endure.
Strong governance.
Clear accountability and careful stewardship of Red Shed’s assets, run as a purpose-driven not-for-profit.
Measuring what matters.
Tracking our progress on people, planet and performance goals, and reporting honestly on how we’re going.
Partnerships.
Working with community, government and local partners to amplify our impact beyond our own site.
Reinvesting in better.
Surpluses go back into facilities, programs and the community, building a Red Shed that lasts.
Be part of it
Delivering all three underpins growth and performance for our athletes and our community.

pages.title: Your Guide to Learn to Row - Red Shed
pages.text:
Your Guide to Learn to Row
Thinking about learning to row, or already booked in? This guide covers everything the booking page doesn’t need to: how the program works, what you’ll learn, what to bring and where rowing can take you. For current dates, times and bookings, head to
adult Learn to Row
or
youth Learn to Row
.
How the program works
Learn to Row is where rowing starts at Red Shed. It runs as a fixed-length program with a single fee, so it’s not a membership and there are no ongoing payments. Programs come in different shapes: most run once a week across a term, while intensives and holiday programs condense the same coaching into a shorter block, and session lengths vary with them. Every listing shows its own days, times, length and price, so the booking page always has the current detail.
We run Learn to Row for different groups through the year:
Adults (18+)
, weekend morning sessions across the term, and an early-morning intensive that covers the same ground in half the time
Youth (Years 7 to 12)
, term programs and short intensives timed to get ahead of the school rowing season
School holiday programs
, a full week on the water for years 7 to 12, from first-timers through to elite youth rowers
University students
, a semester program at a student rate, open to students from any university
Whichever you choose, everything is provided: boats, oars, safety gear and coaching. You bring yourself and a water bottle. Places in every program are capped so coaches can give real attention to every rower.
What you’ll learn
The program takes you from never having held an oar to rowing confidently as part of a crew.
01
The fundamentals
Rowing technique, terminology, body positioning and the stroke, built up step by step so nothing is assumed.
02
On-water sessions
The heart of the program. Coached rowing on Lake Burley Griffin, starting in stable boats and progressing as your skills do.
03
Off-water training
Time on the rowing machine (the erg) to groove your technique, plus the basics of rowing fitness.
04
Boat handling and safety
How to carry, launch and land a boat, look after equipment and stay safe on the water.
05
Sculling first
Beginners learn to scull, rowing with two oars, which builds the best foundation. Sweep rowing (one oar) is an option to explore later.
06
Rowing with others
Rowing is a team sport at heart. We aim to keep you with a familiar group each week, and most people finish with new friends as well as a new skill.
Your first session
Arrive about 15 minutes early so you can find us, meet your coach and get sorted before the session starts. Rowing lives on the bottom floor of Red Shed: go up the ramp and take the internal stairs down, or come straight down the external stairs when you arrive. Your first session covers the essentials on land, an introduction to the boats and equipment, a safety briefing and your first strokes on the erg, before you get on the water. Every session is coached.
Red Shed is on Black Mountain Peninsula, Acton, reached via John Cardiff Close. There’s parking on site, and
Easy Oar
, our cafe, is right there for a coffee after your session.
What to wear and bring
Wear fitted, comfortable activewear that you can move freely in. Avoid loose shorts or baggy tops, which can catch in the boat’s moving parts. Socks are essential, as shoes come off in the boats, and slip-on shoes make getting in and out easy. Pack runners too, for land-based training when the weather keeps us off the water. Bring a water bottle, sunscreen and a hat for morning light, and a warm layer in the cooler months, since it’s always a few degrees cooler on the water. Leave jewellery and anything you’d hate to drop in the lake at home.
There are bathrooms on site with showers and hairdryers, so you can change after your session and head straight to work, or wherever the day takes you.
Fitness and swimming
You don’t need to be fit to start. Rowing meets you where you are, and the program builds fitness gradually. You do need to be comfortable in the water: being able to swim 50 metres and tread water is the standard we ask of every rower. If that’s a concern, get in touch before booking and we’ll talk it through.
Weather
Rowing happens in the rain, and some of the best sessions are the still, drizzly ones. If conditions aren’t safe for beginners (strong wind, fog or storms), your coach will run the session on land instead, working on technique, erg skills and boat craft, so the session still counts and you still learn. That’s where the runners come in. Outright cancellations are very rare, and if one happens you’ll be told by text.
Frequently asked questions
Do I need any experience?
No. Learn to Row assumes nothing. Every skill is taught from the beginning.
Which program should I pick?
It mostly comes down to your availability. If your weekends are free, the weekly program gives your body more time to absorb each session. If weekends are hard or you’d rather get there faster, the intensive covers the same content in a shorter block. Youth rowers aiming for the school season should look at the intensive or a school holiday program, which get you ready before term starts.
I rowed years ago. Do I start again with Learn to Row?
That depends on your comfort. You’re very welcome to start fresh with Learn to Row, and plenty of returning rowers do. If you’d rather not, email our team at info@redshed.org.au and they’ll find the right place to slot you in.
What if I miss a session?
Life happens. Talk to your coach, who will help you catch up within your program where possible. Your enrolment covers the sessions listed for your program, and there are no separate make-up sessions.
Can I join after the program has started?
Yes, programs stay open for enrolment after week one at the full program fee. Whether that’s right for you depends on how far in the program is, so contact us and we’ll give you an honest answer.
Am I too old to learn?
No. Rowing is one of the few sports people genuinely pick up at any age, and our adult programs regularly include rowers in their 50s, 60s and beyond. Masters rowing is one of the strongest parts of the sport.
Is there a weight limit?
There’s no set weight limit. Boats come in different shapes and sizes, and coaches match every rower to one that suits them. The more useful question is mobility: you’ll need to manage the step down into the boat and back out again, with a steadying hand from us where it helps. If you’re wondering whether rowing will work for your body, get in touch for an honest chat. Rowing is about as low-impact as sport gets, and people row well into their 80s, so the answer is usually yes.
My child has just finished Year 6. Can they join a youth program?
Yes. Youth programs are for Years 7 to 12, and Year 7 counts from the moment Year 6 is finished. Students qualify from the school holidays straight after Year 6, so the holiday program before Year 7 starts is a popular first taste of rowing.
Can parents come out on the water with youth rowers?
For safety reasons, only rowers and coaches go out in the boats and the coach’s tinny, so we ask parents to wait on shore. It’s a good wait, though: Easy Oar is right there for a coffee, a matcha or a bite to eat while your rower trains.
Where rowing takes you next
Learn to Row is the start, not the whole story. When your program finishes, you’ll have options:
Keep rowing at Red Shed.
A
Red Shedder Membership
* gives you a weekly allowance of sessions across rowing, the gym and recovery, so the habit you’ve built keeps going.
Development and squads.
Graduates step into development sessions to build experience and confidence, and from there into squads for rowers who want to train and race.
Club rowing down the track.
Black Mountain Rowing Club
is Red Shed’s home club, and where most rowers go when they want to race. It’s for experienced rowers, so it isn’t the step straight after Learn to Row, but keep building through development and it’s a natural place to end up. There are other clubs in Canberra as well, so ask your coach what would suit you.
Not sure what’s next for you? Ask your coach in the final week. They’ll know where you’re at and what you’d enjoy.
Questions? Email us at info@redshed.org.au. We’re happy to help you pick the right program.

pages.title: Your Guide to the 3 Day Performance Clinic - Red Shed
pages.text:
Your Guide to the 3 Day Performance Clinic
Thinking about the clinic, or already booked in? This guide covers everything the booking page doesn’t need to: how the three days run, who the clinic suits, what to bring, and how to make a proper trip of it while you’re here. For current dates, prices and bookings, head back to the
Camps & Clinics page
.
What the clinic is
Three days of coaching built around one thing: making your boat go faster. You’ll be filmed, watched closely, given specific feedback and then sent straight back out to apply it, over and over, until the change starts to hold.
It’s a fixed-length program with a single fee, so it isn’t a membership and there are no ongoing payments. Coaching runs across the mornings, which leaves your afternoons free for recovery or for Canberra.
Coaching runs in small groups and numbers are deliberately capped, so nobody spends three days at the back of a group hoping to be noticed.
Who it’s for
The clinic suits rowers with more than twelve months on the water who have raced, or intend to. That’s the honest entry point, and it isn’t about being fast. It’s about having enough technical vocabulary to use the feedback you’ll be given.
Come solo or bring your crew. Solo rowers are matched into small boats by ability, so you’ll row with people at a similar level rather than being carried or doing the carrying. Crews who arrive together can keep their combination and work on it as a unit.
Most people who do the clinic are masters rowers, and our coaches spend a lot of their week with masters athletes. If you’re returning to rowing after a long break, or you’ve rowed for years but never had proper technical feedback, get in touch before booking and we’ll give you a straight answer about whether it’s the right fit.
Bringing someone who doesn’t row
Plenty of people come with a partner or friend who has never touched an oar. Rather than have them wait around, we run a tailored Learn to Row alongside the clinic, so they spend the mornings on the water too and you’re both free in the afternoons. Mention it when you book so we can plan for it.
What you’ll work on
01
Technique under the camera
On-water video capture, then structured review with a coach who tells you what’s actually happening rather than what you think is happening.
02
Small boat sessions
Most of the water time is in small boats, where technique has nowhere to hide and improvement transfers quickly.
03
Boat setup and rigging
How your rigging affects your stroke, and what to change when you get home.
04
Mobility and strength
An assessment of how your body moves, and what’s limiting your length or your finish.
05
Training that lasts
Honest conversations with coaches about training load, recovery and how to keep improving through your forties, fifties, sixties and beyond.
06
A plan you leave with
You go home with specific things to work on, not a warm feeling.
How the three days run
Day one, assessment.
A yoga-based warm-up to start, then technical small boat rowing with video capture on the water. A mobility and strength assessment follows, then lunch with your coaches while you watch the footage back together. The point of day one is to find out what we’re working with.
Day two, application.
Warm-up, then straight into targeted drills built from what day one showed. Coaches check progress through the session, and lunch is the coaches’ Q&A: training, rigging, recovery, ageing, whatever you want to ask. The sauna and the float beds are there afterwards if you want them.
Day three, integration.
The big boat row. A guided row on Lake Burley Griffin taking in the parliamentary landmarks, in a crew that includes experienced Red Shed rowers so the boat is balanced and moving well. Weather permitting, you’ll pull in at the National Gallery for a look. Then a celebratory lunch to finish, and time with your coach on where you take it from here.
Where you’ll be rowing
Lake Burley Griffin is one of Australia’s best known stretches of water and home to the National Training Centre for Australia’s Olympic rowing team. It’s flat, protected, and it has a laned race course, which is why so much of the country’s high performance rowing happens on it.
Red Shed sits on Black Mountain Peninsula in Acton, reached via John Cardiff Close, with parking on site. Rowing lives on the bottom floor: go up the ramp and take the internal stairs down, or come straight down the external stairs when you arrive.
That’s the lake, and on day three you row a good part of it.
The boats
Our racing fleet is new and race weight: singles, doubles, pairs, quads and fours. Coastal boats are available as well, so you don’t need to bring anything.
If you’d rather row your own boat, you’re welcome to, but email us well before you travel so we can check we’ve got room for it. Racking is limited and we’d hate for you to tow a boat down and find nowhere to put it.
Your coaches
The clinic is coached by Red Shed’s rowing team. Between them they’ve coached Olympic and world championship medallists, led Australia’s women’s rowing program, developed state champions and coached masters rowers to medals at international competition. Just as importantly, they work with masters rowers through the year rather than fitting them around a school season. You can
meet our rowing coaches here
.
Your first morning
Arrive about fifteen minutes early so you can find us, meet your coaches and the other rowers, and get sorted before the warm-up starts. Every session is coached.
Easy Oar
, our cafe, is right there for coffee before and after, and it’s where most people end up between sessions.
What to wear and bring
Wear fitted, comfortable activewear you can move freely in, and avoid anything loose that can catch in the boat’s moving parts. Socks are essential, as shoes come off in the boats, and slip-on shoes make getting in and out easy. Bring runners as well for land-based sessions, plus something you can do yoga and mobility work in.
Bring a water bottle, sunscreen and a hat, and a warm layer in the cooler months, since it’s always a few degrees cooler on the water. Canberra mornings are genuinely cold from May through September, colder than most visitors expect, so pack more warmth than you think you need. If you use your own kit for rigging or measurement, bring it.
There are bathrooms on site with showers and hairdryers, so you can change after your session and go straight into your day. Bring bathers and a towel if you plan to use the sauna or the plunge.
Your afternoons
Coaching finishes after lunch, which is deliberate. Three consecutive mornings of hard technical work is enough load, and the afternoons are where the work settles.
Our recovery hub is included in your clinic fee, so the sauna and the zero gravity float beds are yours to use across the three days. The float bed is a heated bed suspended over warm water, so you get the weightless part without getting wet. It’s all optional. Some people use it every afternoon, some never go near it.
If you’d rather see the city, you’re eight minutes from the centre of Canberra and walking distance from the National Museum. The National Gallery, Parliament House, the War Memorial and the Portrait Gallery are all within a short drive, and the Canberra District wineries are half an hour out. Ask us for suggestions when you’re here. We’re happy to point you at the good ones.
Frequently asked questions
Do I need to be a fast rower?
No. The clinic is about improvement, not speed. What matters is that you’ve been rowing long enough to make use of technical feedback, which is roughly the twelve month mark, and that you’ve raced or plan to.
Can I come on my own?
Yes, and plenty do. Small boat sessions are matched by ability, so you’ll be rowing with people at your level, and the group tends to become a group fairly quickly.
Can my crew come together?
Yes. Bring your combination and we’ll coach it as a crew.
What if the weather turns?
Canberra mornings can be foggy and Lake Burley Griffin can get windy. If conditions aren’t safe, the session moves to land: erg work, video review, rigging, mobility. The clinic runs regardless, and the content still lands.
Am I too old for this?
No. Masters rowing is one of the strongest parts of the sport and our coaches work with masters rowers every week, including plenty in their sixties and seventies. Ageing changes what you should train, not whether you should.
Where should I stay?
We recommend Vibe Hotel Canberra and East Hotel, both of our accommodation partners and both an easy drive from the shed. Get in touch before you book and we’ll let you know if there’s a rate going for clinic rowers.
What if I need to cancel?
Get in touch as early as you can. Cancellations and credits are handled under our
terms and conditions
, and all requests need to be in writing to info@redshed.org.au.
Is there parking?
Yes, on site and free.
Do I need a membership?
No. The clinic is a program with a single fee, booked on its own.
What do I actually leave with?
Video of your rowing, a clear picture of what’s holding your boat speed back, changes to make to your rigging and your training, and a plan for what to work on next.
After the clinic
The clinic is three days, but the point is what happens in the months afterwards. Your coach will finish by talking through where you’re at and what to prioritise.
If you’re local, that might mean a
Red Shedder Membership*
so you can keep training here, or one-on-one
private coaching
to keep working on the same things. If you’re visiting, it’s the plan you take home to your own club and your own coach, and plenty of people come back for the next one to see how far it’s moved.
Questions? Email us at rowing@redshed.org.au. If you’re not sure the clinic is the right fit, tell us about your rowing and we’ll give you an honest answer.
Camps & Clinics
Meet our coaches

Back on the water to apply what you’ve just seen, with targeted drills built from your own footage. It finishes with a wrap-up and clear recommendations for what to do next. Recovery in the sauna or on the float beds afterwards is there if you want it.

pages.text:
How We Coach
Good coaching is the difference between rowing for years and rowing well for years. It’s the thing we spend the most on and the thing we’re least willing to compromise.
Small groups, real attention.
Our camps and clinics are capped so coaches can work with every rower individually rather than address a group.
We film you.
Video is standard in our performance coaching, not an add-on. You watch your own rowing back with a coach next to you, because seeing it is faster than being told about it.
Feedback you can act on tomorrow.
Not “lengthen your stroke”. What’s causing it, what to change, and how to know when it’s working.
We coach masters properly.
Masters rowers are a large part of our program, and our coaches work with them through the year rather than fitting them around a school season.
Our coaches are coached too.
Rowing coaching is a craft, and ours learn from some of the most experienced coaches in the country, so the whole team keeps getting better.
Beginners get real coaches too.
Our coaching team works across the whole pathway, from Learn to Row through to performance. Someone who has never held an oar is coached properly, not parked.
The best water in the country.
Lake Burley Griffin is home to the National Training Centre for Australia’s Olympic rowing team, and our coaches have spent their careers on it.
Our rowing coaches
Between them, our coaches have coached Olympic and world championship medallists, led Australia’s women’s rowing program, developed state champions, and built youth and masters squads from nothing. They also spend their mornings teaching people who have never held an oar.
Meet the whole crew on the
team page
.

pages.text:
The Red Shed Story
Red Shed is the latest chapter in sixty years of Canberra rowing. Our story begins with the lake itself.
From the filling of the lake to the Red Shed
1964, the lake is filled.
Lake Burley Griffin is filled and rowing begins almost immediately. The Kingston Nissen Hut, “The Igloo”, becomes the home of Canberra rowing. Foundation clubs take shape: Burns Rowing Club, Telopea Park School Rowing, Canberra Rowing Club and the ANU Boat Club.
1964 to the 1970s, rowing flourishes.
School, university and community clubs grow, creating a vibrant rowing culture in the nation’s capital.
Late 1970s to 1980s, a pathway forms.
Telopea Park School and Narrabundah College programs unite to form the Telopea Narrabundah Rowing Club (TNRC), creating a path from school rowing to lifelong participation.
Where it began: the old Nissen hut boatshed, home of the Narrabundah rowing club
1980s to 1990s, a rowing powerhouse.
Canberra rowers achieve national and international success, and the ACT builds its reputation on the water.
1990s to 2020s, Black Mountain Rowing Club.
Black Mountain Rowing Club (BMRC) emerges as one of Canberra’s leading community clubs, welcoming rowers of all ages and abilities.
2024, Red Shed opens.
Red Shed opens on the shores of Lake Burley Griffin: the next evolution of Telopea Park rowing, and a world-class facility combining rowing, wellness and community under one roof.
How Red Shed began
Red Shed exists because two people believed Canberra deserved a home for rowing, movement and wellbeing that was open to everyone. Founding donors John and Jeanette Gasson made Red Shed possible through their personal generosity.
John and Jeanette have rowed all their lives. John started at Telopea Park High School in the 1970s, one of the few public school students to get the chance. Jeanette picked it up at university and went on to represent Australia in 1984. They met through rowing and both are still in the sport today.
They spent ten years securing the Black Mountain Peninsula site. Their belief was a simple one, more oars in more hands. The chance John got as a kid from a public high school was rare. Red Shed exists so it isn’t.
Read their story in The Canberra Times
. Want to help put more oars in more hands?

pages.text:
The Recovery Hub
Heat, cold and stillness. Real recovery, guided by our team. No experience needed.
New here?
Recovery is the deliberate practice of helping your body and mind reset, through heat, cold and stillness, so you train better, sleep better and handle everyday stress.
Exercise puts stress on the body. It is the recovery afterwards, not the workout itself, where fitness, strength and endurance actually improve. Skip it and the research is consistent: slower gains, higher injury risk, and a harder time staying consistent.
But recovery is not only for athletes. Heat and cold exposure, and structured rest, help shift the body out of fight or flight and into rest and digest, the state where stress actually resolves.
Never used a sauna, plunge pool or float bed? That is completely normal, and our team will guide you through any of it, any time you ask. We also run guided first sessions with a coach, so your first visit can be shown, not guessed. Just ask at the desk. Most people build up over their first few visits, not their first one.
What’s in the Recovery Hub
A few ways to recover, each usable on its own or together.
Cold plunge
A short, sharp cold immersion. Most people build from 30 to 60 seconds in the water as they adjust.
Eases sore, tired muscles
Sharpens focus and lifts mood
Leaves you clear-headed
Finnish and infrared sauna
Traditional dry heat (70 to 100 degrees) or gentler infrared warmth. 8 to 12 minutes is a good starting point.
Eases tight, tired muscles
Supports circulation and relaxation
A genuinely calm space to switch off
ZeroBody dry float
Lie on a heated bed suspended over 400 litres of warm water. Weightless, with no water contact at all. Sessions run 10 to 45 minutes.
Deep calm, quiet mind
Releases tension, no water, salt or shower needed
Nordic compression
Compression boots that squeeze and release from the feet up while you sit back.
Flushes out heavy, fatigued legs
Supports circulation after training
Easy, hands-off recovery
How to use them together
New to recovery? Try the Red Shed Circuit
Our recommended way to use the sauna and plunge together. A simple, repeatable sequence rather than guesswork.
01
Heat
8 to 12 minutes in the Finnish or infrared sauna. Let your body warm through and breathe slowly.
02
Cold
New to cold water? Start with 30 to 60 seconds in the plunge. Build to 2 or 3 minutes over a few visits. Focus on your breath, not the clock.
03
Rest
5 to 10 minutes to sit, rehydrate and let your heart rate settle before the next round.
Repeat for 2 or 3 rounds. Finish on heat if you are winding down for the evening, finish on cold for an energising lift.
One booking covers the Circuit
Sauna and plunge are the same session, so there is no need to book them separately. The dry float is booked as its own session.
Prefer stillness? Try the float on its own, 10 to 45 minutes, no heat or cold at all, or as a fourth step after the Circuit.
Why recovery works
Exercise puts stress on the body. It is the recovery afterwards, not the workout itself, where fitness and strength actually improve. Regular sauna use is associated with better cardiovascular health and better sleep. Cold water immersion is widely used by athletes to ease muscle soreness and feel recovered faster, especially after endurance efforts. And good sleep remains the single most important recovery tool there is. Everything here is designed to support it, not replace it.
Good to know
Recovery is not recommended for everyone in every circumstance. Check with your doctor first if you are pregnant, have a heart condition or epilepsy, or are otherwise unwell, and never use the sauna or plunge pool alone if any of this applies to you.
Stop and tell a team member straight away if you feel dizzy, unwell or unusually short of breath. New to any of this? Just ask. We are always happy to walk you through it in person.

pages.title: Golden Oar - Red Shed
pages.text:
Golden Oar
Golden Oar is Canberra’s celebration of rowing, held on Lake Burley Griffin. It brings crews, families and the wider community together for a weekend on the water, and Red Shed is proud to be part of it.
The Golden Oar 2026
The Golden Oar is presented by Canberra Airport and hosted by Red Shed.
Not just a regatta, a festival. This year Golden Oar runs over three days for the first time, Friday 30 October to Sunday 1 November, on Lake Burley Griffin. An extra day has been added to the front of the weekend, and the racing has grown with it. Every crew is mixed, equal men and women, and they come from clubs across Australia and around the world. There is more than $200,000 in prize money on the line. An international rowing event, right here on our water.
The format is an omnium, so crews race three times across the weekend and the results carry through. A 1500m buoyed race for strategy and control, a 3km time trial for endurance and pacing, then the 450m sprint showdown to finish. Rankings from the 1500m and the 3km decide who lines up where for the sprint finals.
Away from the racing there is plenty on for everyone else. Entry for spectators is free.
Friday 30 October
Mixed Double Sculls Showcase, new for 2026. A sprint eliminator over 450m at Tarcoola Reach, from 5.00pm to 6.30pm, with heats, semi-finals and finals.
Saturday 31 October
1500m buoyed racing at Yarramundi Reach from 10.00am, with PR3, Masters, Club, Under 19 and Open categories running through the morning.
Sunday 1 November
3km time trial at Scrivener Dam, 8.30am to 10.50am.
Sprint finals over 450m at Tarcoola Reach, 12.00pm to 2.20pm.
Across the weekend
The Wild Swim, a relaxed swim in Lake Burley Griffin open to all ages and abilities, hosted by the local Wild Swim crew.
The Golden Oar Pro-Am, where Olympic rowers team up with community rowers over a short course.
The YMCA Cardboard Boat Regatta, with young crews racing boats they have built themselves out of cardboard.
The RowNation Erg Relay, a chance for anyone to take a turn alongside elite athletes.
A family zone with hands-on activities, face painting and games.
Live music from local artists, afternoon DJ sets, food vans, breweries and local producers, and hand craft markets along the foreshore.
Racing categories for 2026 are Open Mixed Double Sculls, Open Mixed Quad Sculls, Under 19 Mixed Coxed Quad Sculls, PR3 Mixed Double Sculls, Masters Mixed Quad Sculls, Club Mixed Quad Sculls, and Club Mixed Coxed Eight, which is new this year for clubs with sweep rowers.
Entries are through Rowing Manager and close on 16 October 2026.
The full program, race times and entries all live at goldenoar.com.au. Head there to enter a crew or plan your weekend.
Visit goldenoar.com.au
Volunteer for Golden Oar
Follow
@goldenoars
on Instagram for Golden Oar news and highlights.

pages.title: Meet Our Community - Monique - General Manager - Red Shed
pages.text:
Meet Our Community – Monique – General Manager
As a born and bred Canberran, Monique began rowing at a high level in school, which years later and now as General Manager of Red Shed, has provided the motivation to bridge a gap for school kids and the like to start, return or continue to row.
After finishing her studies at ANU, completing Honours in Psychology, Von ventured to sydney where she worked ir the world of start-ups – leading the ship on many ventures where she flexed her strategic skills and love of doing things differently. Eventually, she returned to the nation’s capital to bring her operational brain back nome, working alongside her parents, John and Jeanette Gasson, the founders of Red Shed.
The cool, calm and collected nature she exudes is balanced by a resilient and inwardly competitive spirit, having ticked off some impressive gym milestones – including triple-digit squats and deadlifts, multiple chin-ups, and one of the tastest 2km erg times in the gym. This may or may not have led to her stepping into the alter ego
‘Supermon’.
On the rare occasion she takes a day off, you’ll find her carving up the ski slopes or walking her dog Ziggy.
As the Queen of Red Shed, it’s fair to say the managerial reins are in very safe hands.
Q&A
What movie do you relate to most strongly ?
I am Legend (she asked her sister). Reason pending.
What are you working on at the moment?
Delivering on the mission: rowing for all, wellness that works, and a community that feels like home.
What are you most proud of in your life right now?
Smashing past 150 sessions in RSX and making a bunch of great friends along the way
What’s the best thing about Red Shed?
The people, hands down. It’s a new community, but already something special — and it’s only just getting started.
If you were to marry yourself, which part would you enjoy the most?
Loyal and reliable – a crown-worthy combo
What’s a hidden talent you have that isn’t commonly known?
My skills on a paella pan

pages.text:
Meet Our Community – Jono – PT
Meet Jono, resident Strength & Conditioning Coach here with RSX as we claw our way back through the history books to find out how he went from skinny soccer player to 6 day a week squat-a-holic, how he put 20kg of bodyweight directly on his backside, as well his favourite breakfast treat you probably didn’t know about.
Growing up as a skinny soccer player from Tuggeranong, Jono made himself quite popular at Calwell High, not only for his sporting prowess and devotion to his friendship circle, but also for his striking popularity with the ladies.
Having played top tier soccer for many years, he learned a lot about injury management and prevention, and he turned his own injuries into opportunities to learn and now applies these methods to assist others.
An early riser, you’ll usually find him in the wee hours of the morning underneath a barbell, in the evenings you’re more likely to find him rolling around on the mats at Jiu Jitsu.
As an avid learner who truly cares about delivering high quality information, he’ll make sure that any query you have is met with the utmost care.
We’re privileged to have someone of Jono’s nature and stature in the gym and we appreciate his ever-expanding repertoire of quirks – keep them coming!

What movie do you relate to most strongly ?
Grown ups. I’ll forever be a child at heart and I highly value laughter and friendships.

220kg high bar squat.

Adam Sandler, Jason Statham, Billy Slater & David Beckham

How the community feels like family the moment you walk in those doors.

The endless opportunities each day presents us.

pages.title: Meet Our Community - Denis - Gym Member - Red Shed
pages.text:
Meet Our Community – Denis – Gym Member
As a child, Denis was intrigued with the way things worked. So much so, he once climbed a 2.5m wall in front of his mother and then proceeded to lean forward until he fell to the ground. Fascinated with questions like “why do things fall?”, this you could say was the beginning of a life discovering beauty in the not so common places.
Born in Bosnia during the wartime, Denis escaped to Slovakia with his family at just 6 years of age. As refugees life was not the way most of us would know it. Being misunderstood, melancholic and a deep thinker, Denis learnt lessons early that some may hope to learn across a lifetime. This inner sanctum became the birth place for a life oriented towards discovering the beauty in the mundane and this has translated to a life rich in experiences.
He was a very calm child the moment he got books in his life – a theatre kid. Reading, theatre, music. He wasn’t a sports kid whasoever, though as a teen he was tall and in turn popular in sports favouring height. What movie do you relate to most strongly ?
Tom Fordz – A Single Man; a movie about seeing beauty in places where it wasn’t seen before.
What are you working on at the moment?

The over-intellectualizer, someone to talk to about needlessly over-complicated shit.

At least 5 every session *laughs*. Vroom/Nipples are two.

pages.title: Meet Our Community - Judith - Volunteer - Red Shed
pages.text:
Meet Our Community – Judith – Volunteer
Born in the small town of Lesmahagow, a place famous for its fudge and for being home to the football team that helped bring ‘The Highland Games’ to life, it’s safe to say this sweet and strong Scottish town shaped someone equally remarkable: Judith.
If you’re wondering how our Scottish pocket rocket ended up in Australia, thank her dad—the Chief Dentist for the whole of northern Scotland—who promised 9-year-old Judith a pony if she made the move with the family to Tasmania in 1965. Promise made, promise kept. Giddy up!
Judith loved riding until she ‘discovered boys’ ten years later. She went on to study languages—particularly German and French—at university, where she also met her husband, a professional clarinet player.
Together they built a life full of words and music, raised two daughters, and eventually moved to Canberra. Their girls became bilingual after attending a French school, and Judith carved out a career at the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare. Despite growing up around yachts (not rowing boats!), it wasn’t until a friend from work invited her to try a learn-to-row course that she discovered a new passion. Cue meeting Rodney Palmer, joining BMRC, and—well—the rest is history.
Known as “the glue that holds everything together,” Judith is now just as at home in a boat as she is in her garden. She’s competed in seven “Head of the Yarra” events and spends her time volunteering, rescuing plants from redevelopments, and sipping gin and tonics in between shifts, from shed to soil.
Canberra scored big the day Judith got on board. Thank you, Judith—we appreciate you more than you know.

pages.title: RSX Gym at Red Shed: Celebrating 6 Months of Community & Growth - Red Shed
pages.text:
RSX Gym at Red Shed: Celebrating 6 Months of Community & Growth
6 months in and we’re very happy with the community that we’ve built here at Red Shed and we’d like to take some time to highlight an important transition that we felt was required to solidify exactly how special we believe this place is – and that’s the introduction of a subtle rebranding to RSX; the ‘Red Shed Experience’.
It started with the questions from enquiries about what type of training we did at the Red Shed gym and I felt as though we were selling ourselves short by really saying anything. ‘What’s it like?’ was another. I found myself challenged by ways to describe it, so what I found myself saying was, ‘Come in and experience it’. This was how our 2-session trial was started – and this is where RSX was born.
Now, whilst there’s many things that contribute to this buzz in the community, one thing in particular was highlighted last week when we were playing basketball in a local mixed comp. We were at a get together at one of the members houses one afternoon and decided to form a team. Then one of the team ordered red head bands (can’t say they help, but we look the part). At the end of the game you’re asked to rate the other team and hear any feedback from the ref. The ref then said to us, “What I noticed about your team is it’s so diverse. Like all the other teams look like they’re a team. You guys all look so different, yet you all have so much fun.” This is an example of the comraderie that is shared not only on the court, but in every gym session. If you put everyone in a line up, you’d be hard pressed to pick any noticeable similarities. But I promise you’ll be hard to find any gym around here that has a vibe quite like this one.
Speaking of vibes, we’ve just had a bunch of members hit their inaugural 100 session mark! Iliajia, Nay Nay/Foxy, Liv (Liz), Coastal Kaz, Eriola and Supermon all ticked off this mark recently. Pitbull aka Lina Belina is on 98 sessions. So lots making their century one to remember! One thing we do appreciate is a good story, followed by a good nickname. Whilst we can’t guarantee you’ll appreciate the nicknames as much as we might, we can guarantee the appreciation of how we arrived at those nicknames – which will make for great stories.
We have introduced an Evolt360 into the gym as well which acts as an objective health tracker, measuring everything from your body fat to your muscle mass, your measurements to your calorie set point. Another thing it does to record your bio-age, giving you an age determined by the quality of your internal tissues and cells. The improvement in this bio age has been a real focal point for members and we’ve had some amazing results thus far. This is an added addition for our members to make sure they’re on the right track.
We’ve also added some fresh faces to our team. Jono, one of my best mates who I’ve trained with for the best part of 8 years or so. He used to be a skinny soccer kid, barely 80kg, now he’s the best part of $1.10. On a serious note, he’s an avid learner and one of the most caring and hard-working men I know, so it’s an honour to have him apart of the team.
To add some beauty to offset the beast, Hannah has been a delightful addition in the last couple of weeks and we’ve really appreciated her initiative and dedication to making things happen thus far. So you’re in capable hands with all of us.
Finally, just an appreciation to the people who call Red Shed and RSX their second home (or maybe even their first). It’s been amazing to come into an environment where I was essentially given the keys to the kingdom and a space to create, and whilst I knew it was going to be good, I probably didn’t envision the calibre of people who have made it exactly what it is – and that’s a place to be yourself, have fun, make friends and do it with a smile.
So from us to you, thank you. Let’s keep rising to the top.

for your 2-free trial pass.

Injury Prevention
Injury Prevention
With the weather improving in Canberra comes the natural desire to spend more time down at the boat sheds training in readiness for the summer racing season. With that comes an increase in the volume and intensity of training, but also a greater risk and susceptibility to injury if we don’t look after ourselves properly. It is vital that sessions are bookended with thorough and appropriate warm up and warm down routines.
Warming up and down first and foremost is about injury prevention, ensuring our bodies are activated and readied to endure the stress of training and racing through a full range of motion that we are put through in the rowing stroke.
Continuity of training is key improving performance on the water, so whilst the immediate outcome of warming up and down is focused on injury prevention, there is a clear connection to improved long term performance also.

Rowing Australia has also produced a handy video on the topic with hints and tips from athletes and their professional support staff that hopefully can add further guidance to your individual situation.

pages.title: The Power of Sleep - Red Shed
pages.text:
The Power of Sleep
The Power of Sleep
During sleep, the body engages in critical restorative processes, such as tissue repair, muscle growth, and the release of growth hormone. Adequate sleep allows for optimal physical recovery, ensuring that muscles and tissues repair themselves, reducing the risk of injury, and enhancing overall athletic performance.
Lack of sleep has shown to negatively impact performance in aspects that are critical to rowing, such as reduced muscle strength and endurance performance, in addition to degraded motor skill execution.
Whilst the clear best practice is ensuring you get a full night sleep, here are some additional interventions you can make to your current sleep practices to give yourself the best platform to train and compete.
Naps
Supplementing sleep during the day with a 20-90min nap can improve performance outcomes after a regular night and restore performance decrements to baseline levels after a night of partial sleep restriction.
Light Manipulation
By activating night mode on your digital screens, you remove the blue light which fools the brain into thinking its day time. When this happens, the body stops releasing a sleep hormone called melatonin. Melatonin is natures way of helping you wind down and prepare for bed.
Sleep Banking
Before a big race it’s understandable that you might endure more difficulty falling asleep the night prior due to nerves and anxiety. Similar to the benefit of napping after sleep-restricted night, it is also found to be a useful intervention to ‘bank’ sleep in the days leading up to competition where possible. An extra 1-2 hours per night in these lead up days can help off set a sleep-restricted night prior to competition.
Cold Water Immersion or Cold Showers
Cold water therapy stimulates the vagus nerve, boosting parasympathetic system activities that induce relaxation and stress reduction. Its ability to regulate body temperature, induce deep sleep, and align our natural sleep patterns is supported by scientific evidence. Cold water immersion is best done at approximately 2 hours before bed (ideally in Red Shed’s Cold Plunge pool).

The Red Shed, an ambitious project by the Black Mountain Rowing Club Inc. (BMRC).
The development of Red Shed, a multifaceted facility designed to cater to diverse community needs, has been a journey marked by collaboration, innovation, and dedication.
